# US Depletes Half of Stealth Missiles, Raising China Deterrence Concerns

1,000 Tomahawks Worth $3.6M Each Fired
China Refiner Sanctioned, Iran Crypto Frozen

International\|

Published 2026.04.26. 17:50:18

\|

By Cho Yang-jun

\|Summary\|Save

AAA

![U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent speaks at a budget meeting at the Capitol in Washington, D.C., on Oct. 22. EPA-Yonhap - Seoul Economic Daily International News from South Korea](https://wimg.sedaily.com/news/cms/2026/04/26/rcv.YNA.20260423.PEP20260423005701009_P1.jpg)

U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent speaks at a budget meeting at the Capitol in Washington, D.C., on Oct. 22. EPA-Yonhap

The United States has moved to squeeze Iran's war funding by sanctioning a Chinese refiner that imports Iranian oil, simultaneously pressuring both Tehran and Beijing. However, concerns are mounting that US deterrence against China could weaken, as American forces depleted up to nearly half of their advanced long-range missiles during airstrikes on Iran.

According to The New York Times on Thursday, citing US administration and congressional sources, the US military's stockpile of Joint Air-to-Surface Standoff Missile-Extended Range (JASSM-ER) long-range stealth cruise missiles currently stands at about 1,500 following the launch of Operation Midnight Hammer in February. Roughly 1,100 missiles, or about 40 percent of the stockpile, were used in the Iran strikes. The JASSM-ER, with a range of approximately 1,000 kilometers and a per-unit cost of $1.1 million (about 1.6 billion won), is a missile the US developed in preparation for a potential war with China, the NYT explained.
